tagline: One-lane farm roads follow the valleys beneath the Peters Mountain ridge
intro: Mountain’s Shadow Trail crosses mountain-valley farmland on 29 miles of one-lane paved and gravel roads. Peters Mountain, a 40-mile ridge, is the landscape’s unifying feature. Designated a state backway in June 1996, the route gives access to the Allegheny and Appalachian hiking trails. The drive takes one hour and 15 minutes.

The valley farms were established by settlers living apart from the rest of the county. At Gap Mills, established in 1775, the community’s name joins a pass in Gap Mountain with two former grist mills.
Begin with Peterstown, on the Virginia border across Rich Creek from Midway. Lindside lies northeast of Peterstown on U.S. 219. Gap Mills lies on West Virginia Route 3 east of Union.
notice: Valley farms lie beneath the long ridge of Peters Mountain.

moments.title: Peterstown
moments.text: In 1928, Grover C. Jones and his son William, known as Punch, discovered the 34.48-carat Jones Diamond in Peterstown. The town takes its name from settler Christian Peters. It sits on the West Virginia side of the state boundary, directly across Rich Creek from Midway in Virginia’s Giles County.

moments.title: Peters Mountain Wilderness
moments.text: Sandstone outcrops cap the Peters Mountain ridge, while high mountain bogs occupy Pine Swamp Ridge. Congress designated this wilderness in 1984; the Forest Service manages it. Its forests include upland oak, yellow poplar and hickory, with at least three tracts of old growth. The Appalachian Trail runs about 1.5 miles through the area. Outside the wilderness boundary, a 398-acre Nature Conservancy of Virginia preserve protects the rare Peters Mountain mallow. The ridge straddles the Virginia–West Virginia boundary, extending from the New River through Monroe County into Virginia’s Alleghany County.

moments.title: Gap Mills
moments.text: Gap Mills takes its name from two features: the natural pass in adjacent Gap Mountain and two grist mills once located here. The community was established in 1775. More than a century earlier, in 1671, Fort Henry commander Abraham Wood sent the first recorded English expedition to reach the area. Gap Mills lies on West Virginia Route 3 east of Union.

practical: Peterstown: The backway’s paved and gravel roads are one lane. RVs are not recommended; snow and ice can make the roads unsuitable for passenger cars. (checked 2026-10-11)
